Borrowed from Old Northern French *Kieresburg, Chieresburg, with representing the pronunciation /k/ north of the Joret Line, in turn from Old Norse kjarr + borg.
Rouen (the capital city of Normandy, France, on the River Seine)
Borrowed from Old French *Rodem, earlier form of Roem, from Latin Rotomagus.
Caen (a city in Calvados department, Normandy, France)
Borrowed from Old French *Cadom (later Cahom, Caem), likely from Latin *Catumagus.
Mantes-la-Jolie (a town in Yvelines department, Île-de-France, France)
Borrowed from Old French *Meantes, *Medantes, from Medieval Latin Medanta, from Proto-Celtic *medu + *-anta.
